prompt.context: Our client is a major US television network that is trying to figure out how much to bid for the 2018 Winter Olympics and has brought you in to help figure out the right bid. The Winter Olympics are a huge deal and will require a significant amount of capital to secure the rights. Before our network bids on the Winter Olympics, we want to make sure that we have considered all the right things.
prompt.question: How much should the network bid for the 2018 Winter Olympics broadcasting rights?

clarifying_info.q: What is the schedule for the Winter Olympics broadcast?
clarifying_info.a: 16 days total. Day 1 (Friday): Opening Ceremonies, 3 hours of programming 8-11 PM. Days 2-15: Games, 10 hours/day (Weekdays: 9-12, 2-5, 7-11 PM; Weekends: 11 AM-9 PM). Day 16 (Saturday): Closing Ceremonies, 3 hours 8-11 PM.

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue sources available to the network?
clarifying_info.a: No subscription revenue. The network can keep 100% of advertising revenue. Ad rates are $400K per 30-second ad for prime time (M-F 7-11 PM and all weekend) and $200K per 30-second ad for non-prime time.

clarifying_info.q: How much advertising can be included per hour?
clarifying_info.a: Market research shows no more than 10 minutes of advertising per hour.

clarifying_info.q: What are the costs associated with this deal?
clarifying_info.a: Total production and other costs are $428 million. There is also an opportunity cost of $1M per hour of broadcast time. Revenue will be received with a 6-year lag (time value of money).

clarifying_info.q: What is the company's cost of capital / WACC?

framework: Estimate total advertising revenues from broadcasting the Olympics (prime time vs. non-prime time, weekday vs. weekend, opening/closing ceremonies)
Identify and quantify all costs: production costs, opportunity costs, and time value of money (NPV adjustment)
Calculate NPV to determine the financial value of the bid
Assess qualitative/intangible factors: new viewer acquisition, prestige, cross-promotion of other programming, supplemental revenue opportunities
Form a bid recommendation that reflects both the NPV and intangible upside, considering competitive bid dynamics (game theory)

questions.prompt: Calculate the total advertising revenue the network can earn from broadcasting the Winter Olympics.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment revenue by time slot (prime vs. non-prime) and day type (weekday, weekend, opening/closing). Key inputs: 10 min ads/hour, 2 slots per minute (30-sec slots), $400K prime / $200K non-prime. A strong answer organizes the calculation cleanly by segment and sums to $928M.

math.setup: Segment broadcast hours by prime/non-prime and day type. For each segment: Revenue = Days x Hours/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x Ad rate.
steps: Prime time weekdays (M-F 7-11 PM = 4 hrs/day, 10 weekdays): 10 x 4 x 10 x 2 x $400K = $320M
Non-prime weekdays (M-F 9-12 and 2-5 = 6 hrs/day, 10 weekdays): 10 x 6 x 10 x 2 x $200K = $240M
Weekend games (4 weekend days, 10 hrs/day, all prime): 4 x 10 x 10 x 2 x $400K = $320M
Opening + Closing ceremonies (2 days x 3 hrs, 8-11 PM = prime): 2 x 3 x 10 x 2 x $400K = $48M

questions.prompt: Factoring in all costs, calculate the NPV of broadcasting the Winter Olympics. Is this a good investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify three cost categories: (1) production/direct costs $428M, (2) opportunity cost at $1M/hour for all broadcast hours, and (3) time value of money using Rule of 72 with 6-year lag and 12% WACC (cash flows halved). Net present value should be $177M.

math.setup: NPV = (Revenues - Direct costs - Opportunity costs) discounted at WACC over lag period. Use Rule of 72: 72/12% = 6 years to double money, so 6-year lag at 12% WACC means future cash flows are halved.
steps: Opportunity cost: Opening/Closing = 2 days x 3 hrs x $1M/hr = $6M; Games = 14 days x 10 hrs x $1M/hr = $140M; Total opportunity cost = $146M
Apply Rule of 72 discount (halve for 6-year lag at 12% WACC): $354M / 2 = $177M
math.answer: NPV = $177M. The investment is financially positive.

questions.prompt: What intangible factors and risks should influence the final bid above or below the $177M NPV figure?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates identify: (1) Benefits — new viewer acquisition/audience growth, network prestige, ability to use air time to cross-promote other programming, supplemental revenue from product tie-ins and sponsorships; (2) Risks — execution risk, viewership uncertainty, competitor bids, cost overruns; (3) Game theory — the bid must also account for what competing networks will bid, not just the standalone NPV.

brainstorming.prompt: What intangible factors, supplemental revenue streams, and bid dynamics should the network consider beyond the NPV calculation?

categories.name: Strategic / Intangible Benefits
ideas: Access to new viewers who may become loyal to the network
Prestige and brand association with a marquee global event
Air time to promote other network programming and upcoming shows

categories.name: Bid Process / Game Theory
ideas: Competing networks may bid above NPV for strategic reasons
If the network values intangibles highly, bid above $177M
Overbidding risk: bid must not exceed total value including intangibles
Consider reservation price vs. walk-away price

recommendation: The financial NPV of the broadcasting rights is $177M; this is the floor for the bid
Given meaningful intangible benefits (new viewers, prestige, cross-promotion, supplemental revenues), the bid should be modestly above NPV — approximately $200M is a reasonable range
The exact bid should also account for competitive dynamics and what rival networks are likely to offer
risks: Actual viewership and ad sales may fall short of projections
Production cost overruns could erode NPV
Overbidding above intangible value destroys shareholder value
Competitor bids could be significantly higher, making the win price uneconomic
next_steps: Conduct market research to sharpen viewership and ad revenue projections
Assess competitor networks' likely bid range
Model sensitivity of NPV to viewership scenarios
Define maximum walk-away bid incorporating quantified intangible value
